reviewLegend.verified-scan: Implementation (code/test/config/result) located and read in the last curation scan. Tests were not executed by the explorer.
reviewLegend.docs-only: Rests on repository documentation; no implementing code located, or the capability is documented as proposed.
reviewLegend.needs-inspection: Flagged for a human or a refresh session to re-inspect.

nodes.title: Physical transport model
nodes.role: Advection–diffusion–removal PDE with sources and boundary inflow
nodes.purpose: A 2-D depth-averaged air-quality model: pollutant concentration is carried by a prescribed wind, spread by diffusion, removed at a first-order rate, and fed by emission sources and by inflow at the domain edge. Everything quantitative in PRAVAH is synthetic.
nodes.technical: One fixed-depth layer; piecewise-constant uniform wind (plus one stream-function demo); constant K and λ; Gaussian or raster sources normalised on the grid; open, periodic or closed boundaries per face.
nodes.equation:
∂c/∂t + ∇·(u c) = ∇·(K ∇c) + Σ_j q_j s_j(t) f_j(x,y)/H − λ c
Σ_cells f_j · dA = 1  (grid-normalised sources)
outputs: c(x,y,t) in µg/m³ via the forward solver
assumptions: Single well-mixed layer of fixed depth H
Wind, K, λ uniform in space

limitations.text: Fixed mixing depth, uniform meteorology, no chemistry or terrain coupling
limitations.impact: Results describe an idealised system; nothing here is an estimate for any real place.

nodes.title: Forward solution
nodes.role: FiPy finite-volume solve; truth vs inference solver roles
nodes.purpose: Turns the transport model and an emission/inflow parameter vector θ into concentration fields and a mass budget. The same solver code plays two roles: generating synthetic truth and building the model the inversion uses.
nodes.technical: Backward Euler in time, exponential-scheme finite volume in space (FiPy). All boundary physics is explicit so the budget uses exactly the coefficients of the equation. A ForwardSolver protocol lets another solver replace FiPy for either role.
inputs: θ = emission amplitudes (µg/s) then inflow-basis amplitudes (µg/m³)
assumptions: Truth and inference use the same equations in matched experiments

limitations.text: First-order scheme with large numerical diffusion (K_eff ≈ 1.6 K at the default mesh; 2.4–9.4 K at the Belauri design mesh)
limitations.impact: Plumes are smoother than the nominal K says; sensor-design conclusions describe the numerically diffusive model.

nodes.title: Sensors and observations
nodes.role: Sampling the field at sensors; known Gaussian noise
nodes.purpose: What an instrument would see: the model field read at sensor positions and times, with measurement noise. The inversion sees only these readings.
nodes.technical: Bilinear interpolation on the cell-centre grid at the sensor times, plus independent Gaussian noise with known standard deviation from a seeded generator.
assumptions: Noise is iid Gaussian with known sd
No sensor bias, drift or location error

limitations.text: Idealised sensor model
limitations.impact: Real sensors have bias, drift, representativeness error; none is modelled.

nodes.title: Inverse source estimation
nodes.role: Non-negative, regularised estimation of source amplitudes
nodes.purpose: Given noisy sensor readings and a known transport model, estimate how much each source emits (and inflow amplitudes) and say how well the data constrain each one.
nodes.technical: Because the model is linear in θ, one batch of unit-response solves gives y = b + Aθ; the fit is a bounded (θ ≥ 0) ridge least-squares in scaled units, with diagnostics (effective rank, posterior std).
nodes.equation: min_{q ≥ 0}  ‖(b + A q − y)/σ‖² + α ‖q/q_scale − prior/q_scale‖²
assumptions: Wind, K, λ, H, source geometry, temporal profiles and boundary forcing are KNOWN

limitations.text: A good field fit does not imply correct attribution
limitations.impact: Ill-posed directions are only flagged by diagnostics; see identifiability.

nodes.title: Sensor-placement design
nodes.role: Choosing and evaluating layouts on held-out scenarios
nodes.purpose: Where should a limited number of sensors go? Layouts are chosen on design scenarios and judged on fresh test scenarios, because design-stage scores overstate real performance.
nodes.technical: Random, farthest-point (spread) and greedy layouts over a candidate set with constraints; greedy uses cached quadratic forms so no PDE solve per candidate. Role guards (design / validation / test) and disjoint seeds prevent leakage.
assumptions: Matched model unless a mismatch experiment says otherwise

limitations.text: Small-budget layout rankings are unresolved with 6 test scenarios
limitations.impact: Do not rank methods at 1–3 sensors on the shipped results.

nodes.title: External vs local attribution
nodes.role: Origin tags, boundary-inflow bases, one-way indoor box
nodes.purpose: Separate pollution emitted inside the study area (local) from what arrives from outside (external), and ask whether sensors can tell them apart. Also a small indoor box driven by outdoor air.
nodes.technical: Linear superposition of unit responses gives origin tags that sum to the total field; external input is either an explicit source or a boundary-inflow basis (different units); a concentration-derived external fraction summarises the split.
assumptions: The inversion is given the TRUE temporal profiles and wind history

limitations.text: Synthetic only; F_ext holds for one wind history
limitations.impact: No statement about any real border, place or emitter is supported.

nodes.title: Belauri geography and scenarios
nodes.role: Real geometry under synthetic emissions and meteorology
nodes.purpose: Places the model on the real Belauri (Nepal) municipality: polygon, roads, buildings, facilities, DEM context, national outline. Only the geometry is real.
nodes.technical: Offline preparation turns raw layers into grid arrays and a hashed manifest; scenarios use per-cell study-area fractions and raster sources; forward runs and sensor design reuse the same solver.
assumptions: OSM layer completeness is unknown (a missing road is a mapping gap, not a zero source)

limitations.text: Real geography alone validates nothing; terrain is plotting context only
limitations.impact: No terrain-driven flow; relief starts about 20 km north of the polygon.

nodes.title: Verification, benchmarks and robustness
nodes.role: What was checked, on what data, and what it does not establish
nodes.purpose: Separates numerical verification (conservation, convergence, exact solutions) from matched-model synthetic benchmarks and from model-mismatch experiments, and keeps exploratory runs apart from the final chain.
nodes.technical: Frozen result directories with provenance, a FiPy bit-identity regression gate, mismatch and robustness studies, and an honest ledger of known issues. Nothing is validated against measurements.
outputs: tables, findings with review status, known-issue ledger

limitations.text: No empirical validation; ensembles are small; sd is not a confidence interval
limitations.impact: Treat all statistics as descriptive.

nodes.title: Governing PDE and grid-normalised sources
nodes.role: What is solved, in which units
nodes.purpose: The concentration equation, with every source normalised so its integrated emission equals q_j regardless of resolution.
nodes.technical: Gaussian shapes are sampled at cell centres and divided by their discrete integral (Σ f dA = 1); raster sources use their prepared weights. Emission enters as q_j s_j(t) f_j / H (µg/m³/s).
nodes.equation: ∂c/∂t + ∇·(u c) = ∇·(K ∇c) + Σ_j q_j s_j(t) f_j/H − λ c   [x,y m; t s; c µg/m³; q µg/s; f 1/m²]
nodes.chosen: Discrete normalisation of f_j on the grid
nodes.why: Makes the integrated emission resolution-invariant; the quadrature effect is reported as a discrete-vs-continuous ratio (docs).
alternatives: Continuous Gaussian integral with domain truncation (erf)
assumptions: Sources are steady in space; s_j(t) piecewise constant

nodes.title: Boundary treatment per face
nodes.role: Inflow carries input, outflow exports, tangential faces do nothing
nodes.purpose: Each domain face is classified each wind segment by the sign of u·n. Only inflow faces carry a prescribed concentration (background or inflow-basis amplitudes).
nodes.technical: FiPy's own convection is zeroed on exterior faces; inflow/outflow terms are added explicitly as coefficient arrays (a_in, a_out, s_in) and the budget reuses them. |u·n| below 1e-12 m/s is tangential. The inflow coefficient jumps from 0 to |u·n|+2K/h as u·n changes sign (a property of the Dirichlet treatment).
outputs: a_in, a_out, s_in arrays; budget inflow/outflow terms
nodes.why: Keeps the diagnostics identical to the equation actually solved.
alternatives: Wall (closed) boundaries around the study area (rejected: the polygon is a mask, never a wall)
assumptions: Inflow is a prescribed concentration; outflow has zero diffusive gradient

limitations.text: A nearly tangential wind gives a discontinuous effect of that side's basis
limitations.impact: Boundary-basis results near tangential wind are sensitive.

nodes.title: Decision: fixed mixing depth and uniform meteorology
nodes.role: One layer, constant H, K, λ
nodes.purpose: The model is depth-averaged with a fixed effective mixing depth H = 500 m (nominal). Wind and K are uniform in space.
nodes.technical: H appears only as 1/H in the emission term. There is no boundary-layer evolution, stability dependence or vertical structure.
nodes.chosen: Single fixed-depth layer with nominal parameters
nodes.why: Keeps the problem linear and cheap enough for ensembles and for the unit-response approach.
assumptions: H = 500 m, K = 100 m²/s, λ = 1/21600 s⁻¹ in the demo configs

limitations.text: H, K, λ are nominal demonstration values
limitations.impact: The physical K is never tuned; numerical diffusion exceeds it (see Forward solution).

nodes.title: Decision: prescribed synthetic winds
nodes.role: Meteorology is an input, not a model
nodes.purpose: Winds are piecewise-constant uniform vectors (plus one divergence-free stream-function demo). Terrain does not influence the flow.
nodes.technical: A stream function ψ gives face velocities that are exactly divergence-free per cell; uniform wind is ψ = u·y − v·x. Reversals flip which faces act as inflow.
nodes.why: Real meteorology is outside scope; the experiments vary wind direction and speed on purpose.

limitations.text: No terrain-coupled flow
limitations.impact: Katabatic/channelled flow is not represented; the DEM is plotting context only.

nodes.title: Decision: FiPy finite volume, exponential scheme, backward Euler
nodes.purpose: TransientTerm + ExponentialConvectionTerm == DiffusionTerm − ImplicitSourceTerm + source, advanced with backward Euler on a uniform Grid2D.
nodes.technical: Unconditionally stable and non-negative in practice (negatives are counted in diagnostics, concentrations are never clipped). The upwind variant is selectable through SolverOptions.convection.
nodes.why: Documented as the v0 baseline; implicit stepping tolerates the long steps the ensembles need. (Rationale beyond the docs is not recorded.)
alternatives: Higher-order time stepping or flux-limited schemes (not implemented)

limitations.text: First order in time; observed spatial order ~1.4 in the periodic test
limitations.impact: Finer meshes reduce but do not remove the error; F-016 is preliminary.

nodes.title: Numerical diffusion of the scheme
nodes.role: Effective diffusivity exceeds the nominal K
nodes.purpose: The discretisation adds artificial diffusion, so plumes spread as if K were larger than stated. K is therefore a nominal input.
nodes.technical: For a Fourier mode and wind along a grid axis: K_eff/K − 1 ≈ (Pe/2)coth(Pe/2) − 1 + u²Δt/(2K), Pe = |u|Δx/K. Measured by Fourier-mode projection (periodic, λ=0): +0.606 at 50 cells, Δt=60 s, i.e. K_eff ≈ 1.6 K; the test asserts agreement with theory to 3%. At Belauri meshes (u=1.5 m/s) docs give K_eff ≈ 253–488 m²/s; AGENTS/phase-2 wrap-up give K_eff/K ≈ 2.4–9.4 over the drawn winds at the design mesh.
outputs: excess diffusivity estimate (scalar-speed approximation for oblique wind)
nodes.chosen: Report it separately from K rather than tune K
nodes.why: The physical K is not constrained by any data here.
alternatives: Finer mesh / smaller Δt (reduces, does not remove)

limitations.text: Numerical diffusion dominates the nominal K
limitations.impact: Sensor-design conclusions and arrival times are properties of the numerically diffusive model and are mesh-dependent.

limitations.text: Theory is exact only for wind along a grid axis
limitations.impact: For oblique wind the estimate is an approximation; the robustness run tabulates it for the drawn winds.

nodes.reviewNote: Measurement (Fourier-mode projection, asserted to 3% against theory in tests) vs theory (closed form) are distinct evidence; the 2.4–9.4 range is a documented figure from the geodesign robustness table, not re-derived in this scan.

nodes.title: Mass budget and no clipping
nodes.role: Every run closes its own books
nodes.purpose: Each result carries emission, removal, inflow, outflow and mass-change terms and their residual, using the same implicit boundary coefficients as the solve.
nodes.technical: Concentrations are never clipped; negatives are counted in diagnostics. Tests check closure for closed, periodic and open cases.
nodes.why: Makes budget closure a real check of the discretisation rather than a bookkeeping identity.

nodes.title: Decision: replaceable forward solver, truth ≠ inference roles
nodes.purpose: Every workflow takes an injected solver. Truth and inference roles can differ, and a backend must declare whether superposition is valid before the fast cached route is allowed.
nodes.technical: BackendInfo(name, version, settings, capabilities) is part of every cache key. check_field_result validates dims, coordinates, units and finiteness. FiPy results are bit-identical before and after the refactor (21 files, 0 differ). Only FiPy variants and test doubles exist.
nodes.why: So a non-FiPy solver cannot silently reuse FiPy responses or assume linearity.

limitations.text: No alternative physics solver exists; a surrogate is only illustrated with a test stand-in
limitations.impact: Interchangeability is an interface claim, tested with wrappers and the upwind variant, not a demonstrated surrogate.

limitations.text: linear=True is the author's claim; the framework does not test linearity
limitations.impact: A wrong declaration would corrupt the fast route.

nodes.title: Sensor sampling
nodes.role: Bilinear read-out on the cell-centre grid
nodes.purpose: Reads the field at arbitrary sensor positions and requested times.
nodes.technical: Bilinear weights on the cell-centre lattice, exact for fields affine in x and y; sensors outside the candidate hull are rejected.
nodes.why: Simple, exact for affine fields, differentiable weights reused by the linear operator.

limitations.text: Interpolation error is ignored in the matched model
limitations.impact: Truth and operator use the same bilinear operator, so interpolation error is invisible.

nodes.title: Measurement noise
nodes.role: Seeded iid Gaussian with known sd
nodes.purpose: Adds noise to clean readings; the estimator is told the noise level.
nodes.technical: Noise sd is a scalar or per sensor; draws come from default_rng(seed). In geodesign the sd is a fraction (0.05, 0.15) of each ensemble's signal scale, with common random numbers across layouts.
nodes.why: Gives a well-posed weighted least-squares problem.
alternatives: Unknown or heteroscedastic noise; bias terms (not modelled)

limitations.text: Test noise level was computed from the test ensemble (0.0158 vs design 0.0154, +2.6%)
limitations.impact: A mild independence leak; sensor-design test numbers may be slightly optimistic. Fix not shipped.

nodes.title: Linear superposition and the response cache
nodes.role: n+1 solves instead of one per iterate
nodes.purpose: Concentrations are affine in θ, so readings are y = b + Aθ. b is the zero-emission response; column j of A is the response to a unit amplitude of parameter j.
nodes.technical: ResponseCache computes the n_params+1 solves once per scenario (key includes scenario, solver options, schema, reference amplitudes and BackendInfo) and Responses.operator(layout, times) returns (b, A) for any layout. A 'direct' route re-solves at each optimiser iterate for comparison.
nodes.why: Makes layouts, seeds and noise draws cheap; direct and cached routes agree in tests.
alternatives: Direct nonlinear least squares with finite-difference Jacobian (kept as a check)
assumptions: Wind, K, λ, H, source geometry fixed and known

nodes.title: Decision: non-negative ridge with zero-mean prior and scaled units
nodes.role: Bounded least squares in θ = q/q_scale
nodes.purpose: Amplitudes are constrained non-negative and shrunk toward a zero prior mean; the penalty depends only on α/q_scale².
nodes.technical: Solved by bounded-variable least squares (scipy lsq_linear, bvls). Scales: emission 1e5 µg/s, inflow 0.05 µg/m³ — numerical at α=0, but a prior width when α>0. The prior mean never uses the true emission.
nodes.equation: min_{θ ≥ 0}  ‖(b + A S θ − y)/σ‖² + α ‖θ − θ_prior‖²,  θ = q/S
nodes.why: Regularisation stabilises layouts that are blind to some sources; non-negativity is physical.
alternatives: Unregularised bounded LS (unstable for blind layouts — failed direction F-005)
Non-zero prior from truth (explicitly not used)

limitations.text: Scales act as prior widths; effective_rank also depends on them
limitations.impact: Reported fits must state the scales; raw emission and inflow magnitudes are never compared.

nodes.title: Decision: α chosen on a validation ensemble, frozen, then tested fresh
nodes.purpose: α is chosen from {0,1e-4,…,1e3} by mean regional RMSE of alpha-independent layouts (random + spread) on a separate validation ensemble (seeds 44/9000) and frozen in alpha_selected.json before the test ensemble (33/7000) is run. Benchmarks read the file and record its sha256.
nodes.technical: α=0.1 selected; the criterion is flat between 0.1 (0.01431) and 1 (0.01457), so it is a plateau point. Greedy layouts depend on α, so they are excluded from the selection. Runs with a numeric α and no selection file are labelled 'not selected: sensitivity'.
nodes.why: Earlier exploratory runs chose α=1 after seeing test results; the final chain replaced them.
alternatives: Choose α on the test ensemble (rejected, leakage)

limitations.text: Flat criterion; a small validation ensemble
limitations.impact: α=0.1 is not a sharp optimum.

nodes.title: Identifiability diagnostics
nodes.role: Do the data actually constrain each parameter?
nodes.purpose: Reports numerical rank, condition number, effective rank (whitened, scaled singular values above 1) and a linear-Gaussian std per parameter, plus a weakly-constrained flag.
nodes.technical: Optimiser success is not identifiability. The std ignores the q ≥ 0 bound and assumes σ is right. The flags depend only on the sensitivity matrix, scales and σ — never on the data — so they cannot detect a wrong model.
nodes.why: A good field reconstruction can hide wrong attribution.

limitations.text: Flags are saturated in the geodesign runs and carry no information
limitations.impact: Emission scale 1e5 µg/s is small next to true emissions (0.75–2.25e6), so weakly_constrained fires on every row; 'flags equal matched' holds by construction.

limitations.text: Gaussian std ignores the non-negativity bound
limitations.impact: Unreliable when q̂ sits at 0.

nodes.title: Candidates and constraints
nodes.role: Where a sensor could go, and what may be combined
nodes.purpose: A candidate set with categories and flags, and Constraints (minimum separation, per-category caps). Geographic candidates come from a lattice clipped to the municipality plus reference sites outside it.
nodes.technical: interior (1500 m lattice, IDs stable under cropping), reference_domestic (inside Nepal ADM0, outside the polygon), reference_hypothetical (across the border; excluded by default, only a labelled sensitivity setting). Mapped accessibility is not permission, power, security or connectivity.
nodes.why: Layouts are reproducible by stable IDs.
alternatives: Population- or road-weighted placement (weights exist as options, not the headline)

limitations.text: OSM gaps are not absence of feasible sites; accessibility is only mapped
limitations.impact: Candidate availability is a proxy.

nodes.title: Decision: random, spread and greedy — greedy is a heuristic
nodes.role: Layout methods and what they optimise
nodes.purpose: Random (20 seeded feasible layouts), spread (farthest point), greedy_total and greedy_attribution (add the site that most lowers the design objective). One greedy trace to the largest budget is truncated to every budget.
nodes.technical: A tiny exhaustive-search fixture showed greedy design MSE at 3.7× the optimum (about 1.9× in RMSE; a single fixture, not a range). The tests compare greedy steps with exhaustive search on tiny fixtures.
nodes.why: Fast: no new PDE solve per candidate.

limitations.text: Greedy is not optimal and depends on α and design noise
limitations.impact: Selected sites are mesh- and noise-dependent.

nodes.title: Roles, leakage guards and held-out evaluation
nodes.purpose: Cases carry a role. Layout selection accepts only design cases; α selection only validation cases; evaluation only test cases. Seeds, noise ranges, draws and case names are pairwise disjoint and checked.
nodes.technical: Block hold-out regimes hold out sensor locations; the greedy objective still integrates the block area on design cases (known issue 5). The 'random' held-out points are only guaranteed > 1 m from a candidate (measured min 220 m).
nodes.why: Turns a convention into a runtime error.

limitations.text: Held-out sites and the 'per added sensor' rows for random layouts are weak evidence
limitations.impact: Non-nested layouts; held-out RMSE tracks regional RMSE closely for a bilinear operator.

nodes.title: Design-stage vs test performance
nodes.purpose: Greedy layouts are fit to design scenarios, so their design RMSE is optimistic. At 2 sensors the mean test RMSE is about 2.6× the design RMSE (pooled 3.2×); spread layouts show no such gap.
nodes.technical: Recorded in the matched benchmark (alpha 0.1, test seeds 33/7000, 18 rows per layout). Greedy's advantage over spread is clear from 3 sensors but not established at 1–2 sensors (wins in 78% and 61% of 18 paired rows, difference smaller than the sd of differences).
nodes.chosen: Report design and test scores side by side
nodes.why: Design-stage scores should not be quoted as expected performance.

limitations.text: Counts are modest (6 design + 6 test scenarios, 3 noise draws)
limitations.impact: The sd is a spread of results, not a confidence interval; win fractions are not significance tests.

nodes.title: Geographic design on Belauri
nodes.role: Real candidate sites, synthetic truth, two settings
nodes.purpose: Applies the design pipeline to the Belauri 500 m grid with parameters [road, builtup, external_patch, bg] under 6+6+6 synthetic scenarios, at two noise levels and two settings (interior only; with ≤ 2 reference sites).
nodes.technical: Alpha is chosen per noise fraction on validation and frozen before the test ensemble exists; layouts are compared with paired tables. Rankings at small budgets depend on noise and on the design noise used for selection (F-020, preliminary).
nodes.why: Same leakage discipline as the synthetic benchmark.

limitations.text: Provisional simulation design, not field-validated
limitations.impact: Specific sites and the 'beyond 5 sensors is within noise' statement are mesh-dependent.

nodes.title: Origin tags and the external fraction
nodes.role: Where did the mass come from?
nodes.purpose: By linearity the field splits into local, external_sources, boundary, background and initial parts that sum to the total. A tag is the origin of the mass, not the last boundary crossing — a local plume that leaves and re-enters stays local.
nodes.technical: External fraction F_ext = Σ_w(external+boundary+background) / Σ_w(total), study-weighted and trapezoid time-weighted; it is a concentration share (not a flux fraction) and is None when the time-mean total is negligible. Tags are used only to evaluate; fit_sources receives only Observations.
nodes.equation: F_ext = Σ_w (c_ext + c_bnd + c_bg) / Σ_w c_total
nodes.why: Exact for a linear model and free of extra solves.

limitations.text: F_ext is a concentration share for one wind history
limitations.impact: It is not a property of the place.

nodes.title: Decision: boundary-inflow bases vs explicit external sources
nodes.role: Two kinds of external input with different units
nodes.purpose: Distant unresolved sources are represented by an inflow concentration (µg/m³) on chosen domain sides; nearby ones by an explicit source (µg/s). Never both for the same plume.
nodes.technical: check_no_double_count refuses a basis that represents a region containing an explicit source. In the smoke equivalence study, whole-side bases (one or four) did not reproduce a localised external plume; boundary-basis input removed part of the error from an omitted localised plume (F-019, preliminary).
nodes.chosen: Separate parameter kinds with per-kind errors
nodes.why: Raw magnitudes of µg/s and µg/m³ are not comparable.
alternatives: A single unified external source parameter

limitations.text: Only whole-side basis shapes were tested
limitations.impact: Other basis shapes are unexplored; a basis stands for unresolved distant sources only.

nodes.title: One-way indoor box
nodes.role: Indoor air driven by outdoor concentration
nodes.purpose: A building air volume exchanging with outdoors; it reads the outdoor field and never feeds back. Not part of the outdoor inverse problem.
nodes.technical: Exact piecewise-linear integration of the box ODE; helpers fit an indoor emission and demonstrate misattribution when indoor and outdoor drivers are confounded.
nodes.why: Keeps the outdoor linear structure untouched.

limitations.text: Illustrative box, synthetic parameters
limitations.impact: No indoor measurement or building physics beyond the box.

nodes.title: Decision: exact vocabulary — local, external, international transboundary, indoor
nodes.purpose: Local = emitted inside the study polygon; external = outside it; international transboundary only across a verified national boundary (ADM0); indoor = inside a building.
nodes.technical: The study polygon is a mask, never a PDE wall. The synthetic domain has no verified national boundary, so 'transboundary' is not used there. At Belauri the Indian outline in geoBoundaries is coarse; the external patch is not asserted to be on the Indian side.
nodes.why: Stops local/external splits being read as claims about real borders or emitters.

limitations.text: Nothing in the results establishes international transboundary transport
limitations.impact: No real emitter is identified; classification near the border is uncertain.

nodes.title: Prepared Belauri geography
nodes.role: From raw layers to a hashed grid manifest
nodes.purpose: An offline step turns the raw polygon, roads, buildings, facilities, outline and DEM into arrays on UTM 32644 grids and a manifest of sha256 hashes and licences. The municipality polygon is a per-cell area fraction.
nodes.technical: Boundary verification cross-checks geoBoundaries ADM3 against OpenStreetMap by name, area and bbox. The ADM2 coverage check fails (71.7%), explained but not resolved. The survey-department boundary was not obtained.
nodes.why: No official survey product available.

limitations.text: Boundary is verified against open sources only; OSM and the Nominatim hierarchy are the same source
limitations.impact: Independence is between geoBoundaries and OSM; 28% of the polygon lies outside every ADM2 polygon.

nodes.title: Decision: real geography, synthetic emissions and meteorology
nodes.purpose: Source layers (road, built-up, facility) and an external patch are placed on real geometry, but every amplitude, onset profile and wind is a synthetic demonstration value.
nodes.technical: The external patch (≈ 2.9 km from the polygon, outside it) is a spatial prior, not an identified emitter. About 5% of a local layer's mass sits in boundary cells outside the polygon and is tagged local (tolerance 6%).
nodes.why: There is no emission or measurement data.

limitations.text: No empirical content
limitations.impact: Do not read concentrations as Belauri estimates.

nodes.title: Decision: DEM is plotting context, not a flow solver input
nodes.purpose: DEM, hillshade, slope and elevation profiles are drawn on maps; no solver input reads them.
nodes.technical: plotting_only_check substitutes constants for those layers, shows the Scenario is identical and the concentration change is exactly 0. Relief begins about 20 km north of the polygon.
nodes.why: No terrain-coupled flow model exists.

limitations.text: No katabatic or channelled flow
limitations.impact: Wind structure near terrain is unrepresented.

nodes.title: Belauri forward runs
nodes.purpose: Forward simulations of local and external parts under several prescribed winds; sensitivity to the outer domain and the mesh.
nodes.technical: The external patch reaches the municipality whenever the wind carries it from the WSW side, not under steady north/east winds (F-018, preliminary). Outer-domain distance changes results when the wind reverses. Numerical diffusion dominates nominal K at these meshes.
nodes.chosen: 500 m production mesh with a 250 m comparison
nodes.why: Cost versus resolution; the 250 m comparison covers one wind.

limitations.text: Arrival times are resolved to the 900 s output interval; 250 m comparison for one wind only
limitations.impact: Fine timing statements are not supported.

nodes.title: Numerical verification
nodes.purpose: Checks against mathematics rather than data: uniform field stays uniform, removal-only formula, closed-domain mass conservation, budget closure, steady throughflow, convergence in space and time, effective diffusion versus theory.
nodes.technical: Tests assert tolerances; scripts/verification.py writes the verification table. The README states nothing is verified against measurements.
nodes.why: No observations exist.

limitations.text: Verification of the discretisation says nothing about physical realism
limitations.impact: Smoke-sized fixtures dominate the CI-style tests.

nodes.title: Decision: matched-model benchmarks are an 'inverse crime' and are labelled so
nodes.role: Truth and inference share solver, grid and physics
nodes.purpose: Recovery and design results in matched experiments are optimistic bounds: they show what a layout can do when the model is right.
nodes.technical: The README and validation record state this explicitly. Only the mismatch and robustness experiments probe model error.
nodes.why: Real data would never match the inference model exactly.
alternatives: Generate truth with a different solver (possible through the role split; no alternative physics solver exists)

limitations.text: Most reported numbers are matched-model
limitations.impact: Do not quote them as performance on real data.

nodes.title: Mismatch and robustness experiments
nodes.role: Truth differs from the inference model one way at a time
nodes.purpose: v0: finer grid with smaller Δt, hidden +20% wind speed and 15° rotation, an unmodelled fourth source. Geodesign robustness adds unseen winds, omitted sources, boundary-profile changes and a 250 m refinement study with layouts and α fixed.
nodes.technical: Findings (preliminary): an unknown wind error dominates the sensor-count effect; layouts matched-optimal at 2–3 sensors are not robust (per-case counts mixed); ranking changes are not resolved against noise (F-017, F-021). Known issues 3 and 4 limit the ranking-stability and refinement conclusions.
nodes.chosen: Reuse fixed layouts and frozen α
nodes.why: Isolates the effect of the change.

limitations.text: Ranking-stability metric counts exactly-zero contrasts as kept and has no noise baseline
limitations.impact: Read it as 'rankings were never resolved'.

limitations.text: Refinement re-selection used 3 fine design cases vs 6
limitations.impact: Jaccard 0–0.2 cannot be separated from ordinary greedy instability.

nodes.title: FiPy bit-identity regression gate
nodes.role: Refactors may not change deterministic outputs
nodes.purpose: Default workflows are captured before and after a refactor and compared file by file (volatile keys excluded). 21 files compared, 0 differ; a negative control with the upwind scheme is flagged.
nodes.technical: scripts/capture_regression.py + scripts/compare_runs.py. Two captures of the old code also compared 21 files, 0 differ.
nodes.why: Legacy FiPy outputs must stay bit-identical.

limitations.text: Reproduction on other machines or library versions was not tested
limitations.impact: Bit-identity is claimed for the recorded environment.

nodes.title: Decision: exploratory runs are superseded and never merged with the final chain
nodes.purpose: The first benchmark, unregularised and mismatch runs (α=1 chosen after test results were seen; test seeds 22/5000) are kept for the record only. The final chain re-runs with α frozen on validation and fresh test seeds.
nodes.technical: The unregularised α=0 run is a sensitivity run, not a selected α. Notebooks and smoke configs use α=1 as a demo value. Findings are superseded, not rewritten.
nodes.why: Earlier text calling the α=1 choice 'a priori' was wrong.

limitations.text: Exploratory result files remain in results/ and can be mistaken for final ones
limitations.impact: Always read the *-final directories.

nodes.title: Data-based model check (χ² per degree of freedom)
nodes.purpose: A weighted-residual χ²/dof check that could detect a wrong wind or an omitted source from the data alone. The docs name it as the best next experiment, with the test noise level fixed from the validation scale.
nodes.technical: An attempt exists in the unshipped git stash 'G2-unshipped' (not merged, not rerun). Nothing in the package computes it today.

limitations.text: Nothing in the pipeline currently detects a wrong wind
limitations.impact: Identifiability flags cannot (by construction); the largest risk to any design here is the meteorology the estimator is told.

nodes.title: CLI and configuration
nodes.purpose: The entry point. Subcommands simulate, inverse, benchmark and geo; `benchmark` dispatches on cfg['experiment'] to every study. Configs are JSON, can extend another file, and the CLI can override truth/inference solvers.
nodes.technical: config.py holds frozen dataclasses and loading; configs/ holds representative experiment definitions.

nodes.title: Scenario and data
nodes.purpose: Everything that defines the problem except the amplitudes: domain, sources, wind, boundary, times, study region; plus the optional GIS layer that prepares the real Belauri data.
nodes.technical: config.Scenario and param_table; sources.py normalisation and weights; geo/ (fetch, prepare, regionio, scenarios) with GIS libraries imported lazily.

nodes.title: Forward solver layer
nodes.role: forward.py: simulate and the ForwardSolver interface
nodes.purpose: The FiPy implementation and the replaceable-solver protocol with BackendInfo and capability flags.
nodes.technical: simulate(scenario, q, solver_options) → FieldResult; FIPY default instance; FipyForward variants; get_forward.

nodes.title: Observations
nodes.purpose: SensorLayout, ObservationSpec, interp_weights, sample and observe.
nodes.technical: Pure NumPy/xarray; used both to generate readings and to build the linear operator rows.

nodes.title: Inverse and attribution
nodes.purpose: Unit-response cache, bounded ridge fit, diagnostics, reconstruction; origin tags, external fractions and identifiability report.
nodes.technical: fit_sources takes only Observations; attribution takes Responses and θ.

nodes.title: Design and experiment runners
nodes.role: design.py, experiments.py, geodesign*.py, transboundary.py, indoor.py, belauri.py
nodes.purpose: Layout construction and scoring, the benchmark/alpha-selection/mismatch runners, the geographic design and robustness studies, the external/local study, the indoor box and the Belauri forward runner.
nodes.technical: Each runner writes a result directory with config, provenance and tables; runners are dispatched from the CLI.

nodes.title: Metrics, outputs and provenance
nodes.purpose: Weighted time-integrated RMSE/MSE, run directories that refuse overwrite, JSON/CSV/NetCDF writers and a provenance record (versions, git revision, dirty-state hash).
nodes.technical: Provenance is written by every runner; research-registry scripts live in scripts/ and are never imported by the package.

nodes.title: Tests and verification scripts
nodes.purpose: pytest suites per module (447 tests reported in AGENTS.md; not run here), the verification study, the regression capture/compare scripts and the notebook checker.
nodes.technical: Real-data tests skip without data/belauri/manifest.json. Notebooks 01–06 are user-owned.

nodes.title: cli.py: subcommands and solver flags
nodes.purpose: main() wires simulate / inverse / benchmark / geo; cmd_benchmark picks the study from cfg['experiment'] and passes truth/inference solvers.
nodes.technical: _forwards resolves --solver, --truth-solver, --inference-solver (+ kwargs) through get_forward.

nodes.title: config.py: frozen dataclasses and loader
nodes.purpose: Domain, sources (Gaussian/Raster), StudyRegion/StudyMask, WindSegment, Transport, Boundary/InflowBasis, Times, SolverOptions, Scenario.
nodes.technical: Validation happens in constructors; load_config merges `extends` (dicts merge, lists and scalars replace).

nodes.title: configs/*.json
nodes.purpose: reference.json (single run), alpha_selection.json → benchmark.json → mismatch.json (final chain), geodesign*.json, transboundary*.json, belauri_forward*.json, smoke variants.
nodes.technical: Seeds, budgets, noise and the alpha_selection_file link are set here; `smoke` configs are plumbing checks only.

nodes.title: Scenario and parameter table
nodes.purpose: Scenario.param_table() orders emission parameters then inflow parameters with units and kind; n_params follows.
nodes.technical: The kinds drive scaling in the inverse and per-kind error reporting.

nodes.title: sources.py
nodes.purpose: source_fields, emission_profile, study_weights, origin-tag consistency checks.
nodes.technical: Raster sources use prepared weights; the local origin fraction inside the study mask is checked.

nodes.title: geo/ package (optional extra)
nodes.role: Fetch, prepare, region I/O, Belauri scenarios
nodes.purpose: fetch (bounded cached network), prepare (offline arrays, manifest, boundary verification, border classification), regionio (CRS, grids, fractions, DEM), scenarios (winds, crop, belauri_scenario, numerical_diffusion_estimate).
nodes.technical: GIS libraries are imported lazily; core imports never need them.

nodes.title: forward.simulate and _Segment
nodes.purpose: Per wind segment an equation is assembled once; each step sets the source, solves with LinearLUSolver, and accumulates the budget.
nodes.technical: Boundary arrays a_in, a_out, s_in come from side geometry; stream-function winds give face velocities.

nodes.title: ForwardSolver / BackendInfo / FipyForward / get_forward
nodes.purpose: Protocol with `info` and capabilities; get_forward resolves specs once; check_field_result validates every result.
nodes.technical: Backend identity is hashed into every response-cache key.

nodes.title: SensorLayout, interp_weights, sample
nodes.purpose: Bilinear weights on cell centres; sample() returns readings at requested times.
nodes.technical: Out-of-range sensors and non-monotone times are rejected.

nodes.title: ObservationSpec and observe
nodes.purpose: observe = sample + iid N(0, sd²); noise sd scalar or per sensor.
nodes.technical: Used by cases and by the direct fit.

nodes.title: Responses, ResponseCache, cache_key
nodes.purpose: n_params+1 solves per scenario; operator(layout, times) returns (b, A); on-disk and in-memory caches keyed with BackendInfo.
nodes.technical: Refuses backends that do not declare `linear`.

nodes.title: fit_sources, solve_linear, FitResult
nodes.purpose: Linear route (bvls) or direct least_squares; FitResult carries rank, condition, effective_rank, q_std and scales.
nodes.technical: Heldout sensors can be excluded bitwise; mixed zero/non-zero sigma raises.

nodes.title: attribution.py
nodes.role: Tags, fractions, per-kind errors, identifiability report
nodes.purpose: contributions, origin_fractions, external_fraction, component_errors, emission_error, identifiability_report.
nodes.technical: Tags are for evaluation only; fits never see them.

nodes.title: design.py
nodes.purpose: Candidates/Constraints, DesignCase with QuadForm objectives, random/spread/greedy layouts, role guards, assert_disjoint, held-out blocks.
nodes.technical: Greedy runs on DESIGN cases only.

nodes.title: experiments.py
nodes.purpose: make_ensemble, check_ensembles, run_alpha_selection, run_benchmark, run_mismatch, refine_scenario, perturb_wind.
nodes.technical: Reads the frozen alpha file and layouts of a finished benchmark.

nodes.title: geodesign.py and geodesign_robust.py
nodes.purpose: Candidate table, ensembles, alpha per noise fraction, layouts, held-out evaluation; robustness re-uses fixed layouts and α, builds mismatch truths, refinement.
nodes.technical: check_same_study refuses a config that differs from the main run.

nodes.title: transboundary.py and indoor.py
nodes.role: External/local study and the indoor box
nodes.purpose: Named scenarios on two domains, recovery, special cases, boundary-vs-plume equivalence; separate exact indoor ODE.
nodes.technical: check_no_double_count and seed guards.

nodes.title: belauri.py
nodes.purpose: run_belauri_forward, what_changes, plotting_only_check, outer-domain and mesh tables, figures.
nodes.technical: Reads the prepared region via the manifest sha256.

nodes.title: metrics.py
nodes.purpose: field_mse / field_rmse with trapezoid time weights over [t_exclude, T]; source_error; sensor_rmse.
nodes.technical: Study-area mask weights come from the region.

nodes.title: io.py
nodes.purpose: make_run_dir refuses non-empty output unless overwritten; provenance(config, seeds, extra) records versions, git revision and dirty-state hash; NaN written as null.
nodes.technical: Frozen results under results/ must not be overwritten.

nodes.title: tests/
nodes.purpose: One test module per source module plus solver routing and contracts; tests use smoke-sized fixtures.
nodes.technical: Real-data tests skip without the manifest. Not executed by the explorer.

nodes.title: scripts/
nodes.purpose: verification.py, capture_regression.py, compare_runs.py, verify_notebooks.py, geo_report.py and table builders.
nodes.technical: scripts/ may use the Research Panel; the package never does.
